# Gelabber v0.10.1

Integrated through #543 and #557 (Dependabot's #544 to #555) into `v0.10`
and the version PR into `main`.

One work package and this week's dependency updates. **Feedback**: people
tell the operators of their instance what they notice, in the browser and
the desktop app, and operators answer under Betrieb; visitors without an
account can use a public form. There is one database migration (`0036`;
it changes no existing data). `compose.yaml` passes two new values to
`web` and moves the Caddy and Redis pins. `.env` needs no edit: feedback is
on wherever `API_OPERATOR_EMAILS` already names an operator.

**Back up before the update.** The migration cannot be undone; the way back
to v0.10.0 is the backup from before it.

## Feedback (#543, browser and app)

- **"Feedback geben"** in the user menu opens a dialog: Idee, Problem or
  Lob, a text of up to 4,000 characters and one optional PNG, JPEG or WebP
  image of up to 5 MB (the browser takes a chosen or pasted image, the app
  a chosen or dropped file). The dialog lists what goes along: app, system,
  version, language and the page you are on, without query. Nothing else
  is sent. Closing the dialog keeps the draft.
- **Einstellungen → Feedback** lists your entries as threads with the
  operators' replies, marked "Offen" or "Erledigt", and you can answer; an
  answer opens a done entry again. A reply you have not read puts a dot on
  the user menu and on the settings row. With account mail on, the first
  unread reply also sends you a mail that there is an answer, without its
  text.
- **Operators answer as "Betreiber"** ("Operators"), never with their
  names.
- **Your data export** now holds the feedback you sent with its replies
  (`feedback.json`, images under `feedback/`). Deleting your account keeps
  the entries for the operators without the link to you and deletes their
  images.
- **The public form** at `/de/feedback` and `/en/feedback` is for visitors
  without an account: kind, text and an address, no image. A mail brings a
  confirmation link, valid 24 hours; only opening it delivers the entry.
  Opening it again within the 24 hours lands on the same thank-you page.
  An operator's reply reaches the visitor by mail with its text; the
  visitor cannot answer by mail.

## Betrieb → Feedback (#543, browser only)

- Next to Meldungen, with the open entries counted in the sidebar. Filter
  by open or done and by kind, open an entry (sender, time, kind, text,
  image, what was sent along, thread), reply, mark it done, open it again,
  or delete it as spam. Deleting removes text, image and thread for good.
  A reply to a done entry leaves it done.
- With account mail on, every operator whose account has confirmed its
  address and is not disabled gets a mail for each new entry (a visitor's
  once confirmed) and each reply from its sender. The mail quotes the
  first three lines, at most 300 characters, and links the entry.
- With account mail off, operators still reply to accounts, but not to
  visitors, and nobody gets mail.
- Every action writes an audit row
  (`feedback.list|read|reply|done|reopen|delete`, the entry in the new
  column `operator_audit.target_feedback`); loading an image writes none.
- The app's user menu opens Betrieb in the browser, as before.

## Desktop app

- Everything under Feedback above; Betrieb and the public form are web
  pages.
- **A file dropped on an open dialog no longer reaches the page under
  it.** It was also attached to the chat's composer, or uploaded as avatar
  or banner on Einstellungen → Profil and Profilkarte (#543).
- The packages carry four updated libraries (rusqlite, fontique, resvg,
  tokio-tungstenite, #552 to #555). Nothing visible changes: icons render
  byte-identical, and fontique picks the same fonts on Linux.

## Server and deployment (#557)

- **Caddy 2.11.8** (bundled proxy): request headers are limited to 16 KiB
  (larger ones get 431), a request body or response that makes no progress
  for a minute is aborted, header names with a `.` are dropped, and an
  invalid `Host` gets 400. Both bundled Caddyfiles validate with it.
- **Redis 8.10.2** is a security release. Compose runs Redis without
  persistence, so nothing on disk changes.
- **Prometheus v3.16.0 and Grafana 13.3.0** in
  `compose.observability.yaml`. Prometheus keeps its data format and
  flags. Grafana migrates its database on its first start: going back to
  13.2.1 needs a backup of `grafana_data` from before.
- The API and media images run on a newer `debian:trixie-slim` (same
  release, current packages); the build stages use Go 1.27.3 and Node
  26.13.0. Patch and minor updates in the backend (jiff, aws-lc-rs, zip)
  and in the web client's npm packages.

## Upgrade notes

- The image pins `GELABBER_{API,WEB,MEDIA}_IMAGE` move together to
  `v0.10.1`. `compose.yaml` changes (Caddy and Redis pins, two values for
  `web`): bring the checkout to the tag first. Where the bundled Caddy
  runs, recreate `proxy` after the image switch.
- **Migration `0036`** runs at the API's start. It adds the tables
  `feedback` and `feedback_messages`, a trigger that queues an entry's
  image for deletion, and the empty column `operator_audit.target_feedback`.
  It changes no existing data.
- **Rollback:** the v0.10.0 image set plus the database and storage
  backup. v0.10.0 does not start on a database that has `0036`.
- **No setting:** feedback is on as soon as `API_OPERATOR_EMAILS` names
  someone, and off (no menu item, no settings area) while it names nobody.
  An address listed before its account exists turns it on already, so
  register the operator accounts first.
- **The public form** is published only when all three hold: the landing
  page is on (`GELABBER_LANDING=true`), account mail is on, and
  `API_OPERATOR_EMAILS` names someone. `compose.yaml` passes `web` the two
  new values `GELABBER_ACCOUNT_MAIL` and `GELABBER_FEEDBACK_OPERATORS`,
  derived from `SMTP_HOST` and `API_OPERATOR_EMAILS` (`on` or empty, never
  the addresses). A key that is set but holds no usable value still turns
  its flag on; the form is then published and its posts end in a 404, so
  leave an unused key empty. A deployment that keeps an older
  `compose.yaml` gets everything except the public form.
- **The confirmation token** is in the link's query string
  (`/api/public/feedback/confirm?token=…`), since a page without script
  cannot read it after `#`. The API logs only the path; a proxy that logs
  query strings logs the token.
- **nginx in the web image:** only the two form locations allow
  `form-action 'self'`; every other public page keeps `'none'`. A proxy of
  your own needs no change.
- **Limits** (refusals in `gelabber_rate_limited_total{bucket=…}`):
  - `feedback`: 5 new entries per account and hour; `feedback_reply`: 30
    replies per account and hour. Images count against
    `API_UPLOAD_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_DAY` and the `up` bucket.
  - `feedback_public`: 5 form posts per client address (IPv6 per /64) and
    hour; `mail_feedback`: 5 confirmation mails per address and hour.
  - `feedback_form_hour`, `feedback_form_day`: over all visitors together,
    at most 20 accepted form posts per hour and 100 per 24 hours, counted
    in the database, so a restart does not reset them. Past either one the
    visitor sees the form's error page, nothing is stored, no mail goes
    out, and the API logs `feedback form: hourly ceiling reached` or
    `… daily ceiling reached` at info.
  - At most 200 visitor entries wait for confirmation; past that the form
    shows its error page and the API logs `feedback: too many pending
    entries`. A form post may be at most 64 KiB.
  - `mail_notice`: 30 operator notices and "there is an answer" mails per
    address and hour. Operator replies have no bucket of their own.
- **Order:** the server first, then the apps. A 0.10.0 app on the new
  server simply has no feedback. A 0.10.1 app on an older server hides
  "Feedback geben" and Einstellungen → Feedback.
- **Desktop:** Windows offers the update itself; Arch: `pacman -Syu`.

## CI and repository

- CI's own Caddy download for the Caddyfile tests moves to 2.11.8 with the
  pin; `docker/login-action` 4.8.0 (#546, #548).
- The join-request deletion test no longer races the purge worker: it
  holds the account's purge lock while it looks (#543).

## Open

- No mail left the test machine; mails were checked through the
  in-memory mailer, not a relay.
- The public form was looked at as rendered pages; nobody posted it
  through the bundled Caddy and nginx.
- The app's new parts ran on Linux; Windows was type-checked only. The
  desktop half had no separate review round; it was checked by its tests
  and the parity run. The image upload was not tried on a slow line.
- Left as known differences: the app takes no image from the clipboard; a
  reply to an entry an operator deleted meanwhile shows a toast and reloads
  in the app, the generic not-found text in the browser; the app opens
  `/betrieb/feedback?entry=…` in the browser on the Feedback page without
  the entry (the link in the operator mail is not affected).
- The updated Docker images were not built by hand; CI builds them.
  fontique's font choice was compared on Linux only.
